draft.title: The real number system
card: Rational
a number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, such as 3/4 or −7. Integers, terminating decimals like 0.25 and recurring decimals like 0.333... are all rational.
Irrational
a number that cannot be written as a fraction of two integers. Its decimal never ends and never repeats. Examples are √5 and π.
Real
all the rational numbers and all the irrational numbers together. Every point on the number line is a real number.
The square root of a whole number is irrational unless the number is a perfect square. So √5 is irrational, but √9 = 3 is rational.
draft.remember: Real numbers are the rational numbers and the irrational numbers combined.

a.q: Which of these numbers is irrational?
a.why: √7 is not the root of a perfect square, so its decimal never ends or repeats. √16 = 4 is an integer. 0.125 ends, and 0.666... repeats, so both are rational.
a.clue: Which one has a decimal that never ends and never repeats?

b.q: Which list contains only rational numbers?
b.why: √25 = 5, 0.4 ends and 2/9 is a fraction, so all four are rational. Each wrong list includes an irrational number: √10, π or √11. √25 is not irrational just because it has a root sign.
b.clue: Work out each square root before you decide.

problems.detail: Why (a) says '√7 is not the root of a perfect square', which is muddled. It should say that 7 is not a perfect square, matching the card's rule.
